intro: frames for reshaping what your inner voice says. you bring the words.

formulas.name: talk to you
formulas.why: talking to yourself as "you" or by name, instead of "i," gives you a little distance, like advising a friend. in experiments, people felt less distress and handled stress better.

example.after: hey sam, you're overwhelmed, and you've handled hard weeks before.

slots.label: you...
slots.placeholder: e.g. are tired, and you still showed up today.
ideas: are doing better than you think.
are tired, and that makes sense.
have gotten through hard days before.
don't have to figure it all out tonight.

formulas.name: i notice
formulas.why: putting a frame around a thought turns it from a fact into something your mind said. in a lab study it made harsh self-statements less uncomfortable.

example.after: i'm noticing the thought that i'm a failure.

formulas.name: the friend test
formulas.frame: if a friend said "___" about themselves, i'd tell them ___.
formulas.why: most people are kinder to friends than to themselves. borrowing that voice is at the heart of compassion-based approaches.

example.after: if a friend said "i'm so annoying" about themselves, i'd tell them they're fun to be around, even when they're a lot.

formulas.template: if a friend said "{thought}" about themselves, i'd tell them {reply}

slots.label: how you'd say it about yourself
i'd tell them...
slots.placeholder: e.g. one bad day isn't who they are.
ideas: one bad day isn't who they are.
they're being harder on themselves than they deserve.
it makes sense they feel that way, and it isn't the whole story.
they're allowed to mess up and still be loved.

formulas.name: three kind lines
formulas.frame: this is hard. other people feel this too. what i need right now is ___.
formulas.why: three steps from self-compassion research: notice it's hard, remember you're not the only one, then ask what you need.

example.after: this is hard. other people feel this too. what i need right now is to stop comparing tonight.

formulas.template: this is hard. other people feel this too. what i need right now is {need}

slots.label: what i need right now is...
slots.placeholder: e.g. a glass of water and an early night.
ideas: rest.
a glass of water and an early night.
to talk to someone who gets it.
to be gentle with myself today.

formulas.name: the dial
formulas.why: naming a feeling precisely, including how strong it is, is linked to coping better. "i'm ruined" and "i'm really disappointed" land very differently.

example.after: i'm really disappointed in how that went.

slots.label: feeling
slots.placeholder: e.g. disappointed in how that went.
ideas: disappointed in how that went.
tired.
frustrated with myself.
nervous about tomorrow.

formulas.name: and
formulas.why: "and" lets the hard thing stay true without it being the only true thing.

example.after: i messed up again, and i'm still someone who keeps trying.

slots.label: and...
ideas: i'm still learning.
i'm still someone who tries.
i'm allowed to start again.
that's not all i am.

source.label: dialectical behavior therapy ("and" in place of "but")

formulas.evidence: emerging (a common skill, not tested on its own)

formulas.name: why to what
formulas.frame: what actually happened was ___. one small next step is ___.
formulas.why: "why am i like this?" tends to spin. "what happened, and what's one next step?" tends to move. practicing concrete thinking helped in an early study.

example.before: why do i always ruin everything?
example.after: what actually happened was i forgot her birthday. one small next step is texting her tonight.

formulas.template: what actually happened was {happened}. one small next step is {step}

slots.label: what actually happened was...
slots.placeholder: e.g. i was late to the meeting.
ideas: i made a mistake at work.
i said something i regret.
i didn't get to everything today.
plans didn't go the way i hoped.

slots.label: one small next step is...
ideas: taking a breath first.
sending one honest text.
writing down one thing for tomorrow.
letting it rest until morning.

formulas.name: what i know
formulas.frame: the thought says ___. what i actually know is ___.
formulas.why: a classic from cognitive behavioral therapy: set what the thought claims next to what you actually know.

example.after: the thought says they're ignoring me. what i actually know is they've had a busy week.

formulas.template: the thought says {thought}. what i actually know is {know}

slots.label: what i actually know is...
ideas: i don't actually know what they think.
i've handled things like this before.
one moment doesn't decide everything.
people have shown me they care.

formulas.evidence: strong (as part of cognitive behavioral therapy)

formulas.name: for now
formulas.why: "for now" turns a permanent-sounding sentence into a current one. you're allowed to change.

example.before: i'll never figure out what i want.
example.after: i haven't figured out what i want, for now.

slots.label: your sentence, softened if you like

catchIdeas: i should be further along by now.
